label: H.R. 34

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The Land And Social Security Optimization Act, or the LASSO Act, requires that 10 percent of the revenue generated from certain public lands be deposited into the Federal Old-Age and Survivors Insurance Trust Fund. This trust fund pays Social Security benefits to retirees, their families, and survivors of deceased workers.

affected_groups.effect: Receive funding deposited from public land revenues into the Federal Old-Age and Survivors Trust Fund.
affected_groups.group: Social Security beneficiaries (retirees, families, and survivors of deceased workers)

affected_groups.effect: Must redirect 10 percent of collected public land revenues into the specified trust fund.
affected_groups.group: Department of the Interior and Department of Agriculture

key_provisions: Ten percent of revenue collected each fiscal year by the Department of the Interior and the Department of Agriculture from covered public lands must be deposited into the Federal Old-Age and Survivors Insurance Trust Fund.

Covered public lands include lands under the administrative jurisdiction of the Department of the Interior, including submerged lands on the Outer Continental Shelf, and lands under the Forest Service.
The bill does not authorize the Secretary of the Interior or the Secretary of Agriculture to raise prices for activities that generate revenue on these public lands.
The bill does not reduce the amounts of revenue made available to States, Indian Tribes, territories, or local governments from public lands.
missing_information: Specific total dollar amounts or estimates of the revenue that would be transferred annually

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Land And Social Security Optimization Act, or the LASSO Act, requires that 10 percent of the revenue generated from certain public lands be deposited into the Federal Old-Age and Survivors Insurance Trust Fund. This trust fund pays Social Security benefits to retirees, their families, and survivors of deceased workers.
summary_detail.significance: The bill directs a portion of federal public land and Outer Continental Shelf revenues toward the Social Security Trust Fund without changing user prices or reducing funds allocated to local governments, states, and tribes.
